notes: Boxed marginal note reading 'O.H.M.S.' over 'off 30.4.41' - the ship went back onto Admiralty requisition after IMG_5645's air-raid damage and was released again 30 Apr 1941. Card headed 'No.8 (first side)', labelled 'Cont' - directly continues IMG_5645
black = arrival, same day - transiting the canal
black = arrival. NEW PORT (Mormugao, Goa) - reads 'Morm', matching the period abbreviation for Mormugao rather than Mombasa ('Momb', which appears distinctly two rows later)

UNCERTAIN - black = arrival. Reads 'Sc.L.' or 'Lc.L.'; doesn't match any code in ports.csv. Given the next few calls are all UK/convoy waypoints (Halifax, Loch Ewe), this is likely a Scottish location, but not confidently identified
red = sailing, carried from the unresolved 'Sc.L.' arrival above
black = arrival - Loch Ewe, a major WWII convoy assembly anchorage

UNCERTAIN - black = arrival. The abbreviation appears to wrap awkwardly across the row boundary on the card (part of 'Rds' reads as if written on the following row); resolved against ports.csv's existing 'Methil Roads' (code 'Meth Rds') rather than transcribed as two separate calls

black = arrival - the Humber-mouth reporting point near Hull

WARTIME INCIDENT - a run of blue paragraph notes reads (approximately) 'Holed by collision' with a reference '18/25 L[?]', and separately 'the collision 15/10' and 'the damage [from the] collision'. This is the ship's second reported wartime damage incident (after IMG_5645's air raid). Taken together with the entries below, the ship was in collision around 15 Oct 1941 and required repairs

Blue note: 'Left Loch Ewe 19/10 for Clyde' - heading to the Clyde (Glasgow shipbuilding/repair area) after the collision, '...for repairs' per an adjoining blue note dated around 6 Oct/21-24 (uncertain reading)

black/red = arrival at the Clyde, corroborated by a blue note '(Glas) Arr. Clyde 21/10' and a red citation 'Clyde 21/10' - genuinely uncertain which colour is the 'real' citation vs. the clerk's own working note, but the date and place are consistent across all three
UNCERTAIN reading - red, same day as the Clyde arrival, reads 'Sail of B' which is most likely 'Tail of B' (Tail of the Bank, the Clyde anchorage used elsewhere on this ship's cards) misread

Blue notes: 'Glas[gow] 21/10', 'Glasgow 24/10', '(Lo.) 29/10' - the ship's movements around the Clyde/Glasgow repair yards through late October are logged in blue rather than the normal black/red citation columns; not confidently resolved into discrete port_raw/date pairs, flagged as a block rather than forced
red = 'Glas 30/10'; black = 'Clyde 30/10' immediately after - both citing the same return to the Clyde area
Blue note: 'Left Glas[gow] 30/10' - departing the repair yard

UNCERTAIN - red, reads approximately 'Clyde 30/10 - 1/11'; a further red 'Nov[?] 4' sits alongside. Genuinely hard to disentangle from the entries either side; kept as a single flagged citation rather than split further
black = arrival, annotated '(NS)' beneath - most likely 'New South Wales' distinguishing this Sydney from Sydney, Nova Scotia, though that reading isn't certain

red = sailing, carried from the unresolved 'mble' arrival
